description: Es un sistema inteligente que mapea un área midiendo oxígeno, humedad del ambiente y del suelo, tipo de tierra y cantidad de luz. Un asistente de IA analiza cada zona y genera recomendaciones concretas para optimizarla, ya sea para cultivo o terraformación de un ecosistema, tanto en campos abiertos como en cúpulas cerradas dando ael astronauta el apoyo necesario a la mano para la terraformación del terreno.
summary:
TerraFarm is a digital system available on the web and Android  and iOS mobile devices, designed to support agricultural planning, analysis, and management through scientific and technological information. Although its first version focuses on Costa Rica, its adaptable architecture allows expansion to other regions worldwide, depending on NASA data availability and local agricultural needs.

The platform analyzes temperature, soil characteristics, natural phenomena, and market conditions to provide recommendations for crop selection, planting, and maintenance. It also proposes crop rotation strategies that help preserve soil fertility, maintain nutrient balance, and reduce soil depletion across different agricultural fields.

TerraFarm includes geographic visualization, crop monitoring, and farm management tools. Its database integrates information from NASA and governmental and private research institutions, facilitating data storage and continuous updates.

Through its intuitive interface, farmers with different levels of technological experience can easily access relevant information. In this way, TerraFarm aims to democratize agricultural knowledge, improve decision-making, and promote efficient, sustainable, and adaptable farming practices across different regions of the world.
details:
TerraFarm is an agricultural decision-support system designed to make scientific information easier for farmers to understand and use. Its initial implementation focuses on Costa Rica, but its data-oriented design is intended to support future adaptation to other regions where relevant NASA observations, local agricultural information, and suitable crop data are available.

Our project addresses a practical challenge: selecting a crop is not enough to maintain productive farmland over time. Growers also need to consider what was planted previously, soil conditions, changing rainfall and temperature, water availability, environmental risks, and local market context. TerraFarm brings these considerations together in a geographic, farmer-oriented workflow.

The system is designed to help users explore a territory, review available environmental information, compare crop requirements, consider rotation alternatives, and organize farm and planting records. Crop rotation is an important part of our approach because a well-chosen sequence of crops can help support nutrient cycling, soil cover, and long-term soil health. Recommendations must still account for crop type, previous planting, local soil conditions, and agronomic advice; satellite observations alone cannot determine soil fertility.

Our scientific approach considers NASA resources such as POWER for meteorological information, SMAP for soil moisture, GPM for precipitation, and other Earth-observation products where relevant, combined with Costa Rican statistical, geographic, and agricultural references. We aim to explain where each data point comes from, how current it is, and what its limitations are.

The prototype's documented technology stack includes React, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js/TypeScript data extractors, shared validation schemas, and planned integration with Supabase and Algolia. The current project documentation describes demonstration interfaces and some simulated service adapters; complete live data integration, scientifically validated crop-suitability calculations, and full production deployment are still development goals. TerraFarm is intended to be accessible through web and mobile browsers, including on iOS devices. No specialized agricultural hardware is documented as necessary for the browser prototype; the supplied documentation does not independently establish a native iOS app or operational drone integration.

Our creative contribution is the connection between globally available Earth-observation information, region-specific agricultural knowledge, crop history, and clear explanations that farmers can act upon. The design prioritizes accessibility, understandable navigation, data traceability, agricultural relevance, and the possibility of future international expansion.

The expected impact is better-informed planting and soil-management decisions, not an unverified promise of higher yields or guaranteed savings. Our next steps are to complete and test the live data workflows, review rotation logic with agronomic expertise, and evaluate usability and outcomes through real farmer feedback. TerraFarm's goal is to turn complex information into practical support for more resilient and sustainable agriculture.
